A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the two VfPho isoforms are differentially expressed during seed development, with Phol transcripts being predominant in the early seed stages, and with Pho2 transcripts becoming predominant in cotyledons during the later stages.

the Pho2 gene product is involved in starch degradation during the early phases of seed development, whereas Phol is the main isoform in cotyledons during the later stages of seed development and in mature seeds.

the two isoforms are expressed in different organs and tissues and are regulated by different mechanisms, and that they are not only important in starch metabolism but also in other metabolic processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pho2 gene is expressed at a high level in all seed parts throughout seed maturation.
the Pho2 and Phol genes are expressed in a tissue-specific manner, and their expression patterns correlate with the accumulation of starch in developing seed coats and cotyledons.
the two isoforms of VfGP have distinct expression patterns in the developing seed, and that Phol is the major isoform expressed in the developing seed coat, while Pho2 is expressed in the cotyledons.
